items.finding: Rounding or a corrected common odds ratio might resolve the discrepancy.
items.resolution: The lower- and upper-cutpoint rounding ranges, 3.391-3.918 and 5.260-5.311, are mutually disjoint and exclude 19.918. The printed probabilities cannot identify any single replacement common proportional odds ratio under inverse-link-of-linear-LSmean prediction using the same model and covariate weights.

items.finding: Population-averaged GEE or marginalization necessarily explains the discrepancy.
items.resolution: A constructive five-stratum proportional-odds example with common OR 19.918 reproduces all six published benzodiazepine probability cells when probabilities are averaged first. This proves that the mismatch alone does not establish a wrong coefficient. The paper describes applying the inverse link to LSmeans instead; its actual implementation cannot be inferred from the counterexample.

items.finding: The pending 354 proposal asserts a corrected stimulant-first ordering and says the other rows roughly reconstruct their reported odds ratios.
items.resolution: Removed the corrected ordering from the proposed statement, magnitude, reasoning, anchor and change explanation. No upper-cutpoint ratio in the six Table 4 rows reconstructs its printed OR within conservative three-decimal rounding bounds. Retain printed coefficients and probabilities, and explain the limited reconstruction result without substituting an effect estimate.
